data.body:
Change 3063 merged as f5f666702b4. It was rebased onto S5 (754994fd6c5); the only conflicts were the CHANGELOG.md and release-notes.md entries, and both entries are kept. Votes: LLM-Review +1, with 2 advisories (see the note below), and Verified +1. `make verify` on the rebased tree exited 0 (19823 passed, 87 skipped).

AC evidence, checked on the merged tree:
- AC1 and AC2: both greps print nothing.
- AC3 and AC4: `tests/unit/test_bridge_runner_spawn.py` has 19 tests and all pass. They include the import-site reaper test and the real child-plus-`sleep 30`-grandchild timeout test. `scripts/check_orphaned_load.py` is clean.
- AC5: `docs/exit-codes.md` contains "produced once, in the engine child".
- AC6: `make verify` exited 0.

The first `make verify` run found 2 more consumers, both fixed before push:
- `tests/scripts/test_reconcile_bridge_push_retry.py`: its `rebar` PATH stub is now the harness `run_bridge` with `STUB_MUTATE=0`.
- `test_bridge_primary_workflow_heldout.py`: it requires the user-guide phrase "`dry-run` to canonical preview", which the new paragraph keeps.

File impact is 14 paths and matches the merged diff exactly.

LLM-Review advisory: an exit-0 engine run with an unknown or duplicated `BRIDGE_STATE:` marker is classified as converged and delivered. The old `legacy_exit` walk did the same, since exit 0 matched CONVERGED first, so this is not a regression.
